spec.title: Accepted requests per second (202)
spec.description: Answers with status 202 per second, split by counter mode (hot/off), tenants and phase. Prediction: over phase, hot with 1 tenant tops out near 300/s, 10 tenants near 2000-3000, 100 and 1000 tenants near the no-counter line (about 3500-4000). Surprising: hot with 1 tenant above 600/s, or hot with 1000 tenants far below off. Metric k6_b4_resp_202_total is added by this experiment's script.js (exists after a k6 run).

spec.title: Latency p50 and p99 (client side)
spec.description: k6 http_req_duration quantiles. Prediction: under phase p50 about 5-7 ms for every cell (no queue); over phase with 1 hot tenant the p50 climbs to seconds (queue on one row lock), 1000 tenants stays near the under-phase value. Surprising: under-phase latency that differs between 1 and 1000 tenants.

spec.title: Not accepted (%)
spec.description: 100 x (1 - accepted / all answers). In the over phase with few tenants this is the pool timeout (503) after 2 s waiting for a connection. Uses k6_b4_resp_202_total (added by this experiment). Surprising: errors in an under run.

spec.expr: 100 * (1 - sum by (counter, tenants, phase)(rate(k6_b4_resp_202_total[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (counter, tenants, phase)(rate(k6_http_reqs_total[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Postgres sessions by wait event
spec.description: pg_stat_activity_count from postgres-exporter (scraped every 1 s), only sessions that are waiting. Look for Lock / transactionid (a writer waiting for another writer's row lock) and IO / WALSync (waiting for the commit flush). Prediction: with 1 hot tenant about 20+ sessions in Lock/transactionid, near 0 for off and for 1000 tenants. Surprising: lock waits with COUNTER_MODE=off.

spec.title: Sessions by state
spec.description: Active = running a query (or waiting on a lock inside it), idle in transaction = holding a lock between statements (the API round trips between BEGIN, INSERT, UPDATE and COMMIT). Surprising: many idle-in-transaction sessions would mean the server, not Postgres, is the slow part.

spec.title: Counter UPDATE latency (includes the lock wait)
spec.description: ep_pg_counter_update_seconds, added by this experiment (server side, only COUNTER_MODE=hot). This is where the wait shows up. Prediction: p50 well below 1 ms with 1000 tenants, hundreds of ms or more with 1 tenant. The top bucket is 5 s: a value at the cap means 'at least that'.

spec.title: Pool: waiting requests and wait time p99
spec.description: Requests waiting for a free pool connection (max over the scrape, in count) and p99 wait time (in seconds, see the legend). Lock waiters keep their pool connection, so the pool drains and the queue moves into the API. Surprising: no pool queue while the lock-wait panel is full.

spec.title: Commits and counter-row updates per second
spec.description: pg_stat_database rates. In hot mode every committed request is one commit and one counter-row update (tup_updated), so both follow accepted/s. Surprising: tup_updated far from the commit rate in hot mode, or any updates with off.

spec.title: Locks by mode and deadlocks
spec.description: pg_locks_count by mode (it has no granted/waiting label, so it counts both; use the wait-event panel for who is waiting). Deadlocks per second must stay 0: only one row is locked per transaction, so there is nothing to deadlock on.

spec.title: CPU busy by pinned group (%)
spec.description: 100 x (1 - idle) over the cores of each group (variables cpu_server, cpu_postgres, cpu_k6, cpu_monitoring). The core claim of B4: with 1 hot tenant the collapse happens while server and Postgres are far from 100%. Surprising: Postgres cores near 100% in the 1-tenant run.

spec.title: Postgres container CPU (cores)
spec.description: Cgroup CPU of the Postgres container (limit 2 cores). Exported by infra/scripts/pg-container-exporter.sh, which run.sh starts. Empty panel = the exporter did not start (see pg-exporter.log).

spec.title: Server process CPU (cores)
spec.description: Node process CPU (user + system). Pinned to 2 cores, so 2.0 is the ceiling.

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations per second
spec.description: Must be 0 in under runs. In over runs with 1 hot tenant it may be above 0 because all VUs wait for slow answers (that is a finding, not a generator fault: check the k6 CPU panel).

spec.title: Requests in flight and event-loop delay
spec.description: In flight = requests the server has accepted but not answered. Event-loop delay p99 (seconds) must stay small, otherwise the server itself is the bottleneck and not the lock.

spec.title: DB errors by type per second
spec.description: ep_db_errors_by_type_total. Expect pool_timeout in over runs with few hot tenants. Surprising: statement timeouts or deadlock errors.

spec.title: 1. The verdict: does throughput follow the tenant count?
2. The mechanism: sessions waiting for the row lock
3. Resource view: low CPU while latency is high
EventPulse B4 - Lock contention with a hot row
